senses.definition: Jeremiah = "whom Jehovah has appointed"
the major prophet,  son of Hilkiah of the priestly family in Anathoth; author of the prophetic book bearing his name
a man of Libnah and father of Hamutal the wife of king Josiah
a Gadite who joined David at Ziklag
a Manassehite,  one of the mighty men of valour of the Transjordanic half tribe of Manasseh
a Gadite and warrior of David
a warrior of David
a priest who joined Nehemiah in the covenant ceremony
a priest also in the time of Nehemiah; maybe same as 7
father of Jaazaniah the Rechabites

senses.definition: (b. h.) pr. n. m. Jeremiah,

J. the prophet. Pesik. Dibré, p. 114ᵇ י׳ ר̇ם̇ י̇ה̇ he is named J., because in his days the Lord (Shekhinah) moved from place to place; Yalk. Jer. 257 י׳ י̇ר̇ם̇ י̇ה̇. Ib. … י׳ שבימיו א̇ר̇י̇מ̇י̇ן̇ he is called J., because in his days the Temple became deserted; Koh. R. beg., v. אֱירֶימִיאָה. Meg. 14ᵇ. Snh. 95ᵃ; a. v. fr.—(ספר) ר׳ the Book of Jeremiah. B. Bath. 14ᵇ

name of several Amoraim, esp. R. J., pupil of R. Zera. Ib. 23ᵇ ועל דא אפקוה לר׳ י׳ וכ׳ for this (burlesque question) they ejected R. J. from college. Ib. 165ᵇ עיילוה לר׳ י׳ וכ׳ upon this (reply) they reinstated R. J.—Y. M. Kat. III, 81ᵈ bot.; a. fr.—V. Fr. M’bo p. 108ᵃ; 118ᵇ
v. sub רמה.

senses.definition: n.pr.m. (? י׳ looseneth, sc. the womb? cf. Assyrian ša kirimmaša rummû, whose womb is loosened DlHWB 623);—

136 proph., son of Ḥilḳiah, of priestly family in ʿAnathôth: יִרְמְיָ֫הוּ Je 1:1, 11; 29:27; 36:1, 4(×2) + 116 times Je, + 2 Ch 35:25; 36:12, 21, 22 (יר׳ הַנָּבִיא Je 21:2 + often); -יָה Je 27:1; 28:5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 15; 29:1 Ezr 1:1; Dn 9:2; Ἰερεμίας.
יִרְמְיָ֫הוּ, of Libnah, father of Josiah’s wife, 2 K 23:31; 24:18 = Je 52:1, Ἰερεμίας.
-יָ֫הוּ Gadite, David’s time 1 Ch 12:13, Ιερεμεια, 𝔊L Ιεραμαου. The foll. all -יָה, 𝔊 Ἰερεμία(ς), Ἰερμία(ς), etc.:
Manassite 1 Ch 5:24.
Benjamite 12:4.
Gadite 12:10.
priestly name: Ne 12:1, 2.
Ne 10:3, perhaps = 12:34.
